title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-liam-nguyen
content:
Context:
- PR: refactor/kv-cache-batching (GH #4721) — main goal: decouple KV cache eviction from batch boundaries and reduce per-request latency jitter.
- Author: @morgan-lee. Target: reduce 99p latency spikes observed under mixed-length workloads.
- Quick note: this is still WIP; lots of TODOs and missing tests. Leaving detailed review notes for follow-ups.

High-level comments (stretch goal stuff):
- I like the direction of separating eviction policy from batching; surface area is contained to cache/* and runtime/batching/*.
- Concern: concurrency model changes — need to be explicit about lock ordering to avoid deadlocks across cache and scheduler.
- Suggest adding a short sequence diagram in PR description for request lifecycle (enqueue -> batch assemble -> kv-lookup -> eviction -> evict callbacks -> respond). Will help reviewers.

Review checklist (things I touched locally):
- FUNCTIONAL / correctness:
  - [ ] Validate correctness under edge case: single-token long-running streams (simulate many small seqs interleaved with big seqs).
  - [x] Verified basic unit tests for cache eviction policy (tests/test_kv_cache_eviction.py) — currently passes locally.
  - [ ] Add a regression test that replays the real trace used to produce spikes (see INF-1234).

- PERFORMANCE:
  - [x] Ran microbench: tools/bench/kv_cache_bench.py against x8 GPU instance. Results: mean latency down ~6%, 99p unchanged for synthetic uniform lengths.
  - [ ] Need long-tail test using mixed-length workload (script: tools/perf/mixed_length_replay.py).
  - [ ] Add CI perf job (non-blocking): nightly/run-perf-kv-cache-batching.

- SAFETY / ROLLING OUT:
  - [ ] Add feature flag gate (experiment.kv_cache_eviction_v2) and default off for dedicated customers.
  - [ ] Add metrics: eviction_count, eviction_latency_ms, eviction_reason (capacity|staleness|size).
  - [ ] Ensure fallback to v1 policy on OOM or assertion failure.

- TESTS / QA:
  - [ ] Unit tests for race conditions: simultaneous eviction + batch assembly (create TestEvictionRaceCondition).
  - [ ] Integration test with runtime: tests/integration/test_kv_cache_inference.py (mocked scheduler).
  - [x] Added simple snapshot assertions for eviction metrics in tests/test_kv_cache_metrics.py.

Files of interest (quick pointers):
- cache/kv_store.py — main store (lots of changes).
- cache/eviction_policy.py — new v2 policy (mostly algorithmic).
- runtime/batcher.py — small touchpoints, changed interface for get_kv_prefixes().
- runtime/scheduler.py — subtle change: now calls cache.maybe_evict() inside critical section. THIS IS THE RISKY PART.

Specific inline comments / suggested code changes:
1) cache/kv_store.py: around line 120: acquiring store_lock then calling out to scheduler (store.lock -> scheduler.enqueue) could deadlock if scheduler also tries to acquire store_lock later. Recommend reversing call order or using non-blocking callbacks.
   - Proposed: introduce a thin EvictionNotification object queued to scheduler instead of direct call.

2) eviction_policy.py: algorithm looks good but not tuned for token-size heterogeneity. Add an additional heuristic: weight entries by avg_token_size * recency_score. This should reduce evicting small but frequently used prefixes.

3) runtime/batcher.py: get_kv_prefixes() now returns list of prefixes but caller expects stable iteration; ensure the function returns an immutable snapshot (copy) to avoid iterator invalidation under concurrent mutation.

4) scheduler.py change: "call cache.maybe_evict() inside critical section" — please annotate with comment why we need to hold the lock; if possible, reduce critical section to just compute eviction candidates and perform eviction outside.

Local repro notes / commands I ran:
- unit tests: pytest tests/unit/test_kv_store.py::TestKVStore::test_basic_eviction -q
- microbench: python tools/bench/kv_cache_bench.py --model llama-3-small --iter 1000 --batch-size 8
- perf replay: python tools/perf/mixed_length_replay.py --trace data/traces/mixed_2024-09-30.json --out perf/out.json
- memory profiler: PYTHONMALLOC=malloc python -m memory_profiler runtime/scheduler.py

Questions for author / TODOs to ask on PR:
- Why was maybe_evict() moved into scheduler critical section? Was there a specific concurrency bug you were addressing? Link to reproducer would help.
- Can you add a brief note on expected metric deltas (eviction_count, latencies) and which dashboards to watch after rollout?
- Are we intentionally making eviction decisions based on compressed size vs token count? Need clarity (comment in code).

Follow-ups / post-merge work (tickets):
- Create INF-1300: nightly perf job + alerting on 99p regressions for kv-cache path.
- Create INF-1301: add rollback integration test that toggles feature flag and validates no request loss.
- Add a short runbook in Confluence: "KV cache eviction v2 rollouts" (link in linked_artifacts).

Risk assessment / recommended rollout plan:
- Stage 1: keep behind experiment flag, deploy to canary region with 5% traffic. Watch eviction_count and 99p latency for 24h.
- Stage 2: expand to 25% if no regressions for 24h, enable A/B with v1 for 10% of requests for additional 48h.
- Stage 3: full rollout with automated rollback if alert triggers (threshold: 99p latency +10% vs baseline).

Misc small notes (notes-to-self style):
- Consider adding docs/examples in docs/ops/kv-cache.md — quick snippet showing how to tune feature flag.
- Talk to SRE (Samira) about number of eviction hooks fired per second under current prod load. Maybe tune backoff.
- Check model perf impact: small models > large models differently; add model-dim stratification in nightly perf.

Final quick summary (what needs to land in PR before merging):
- [ ] Rework scheduler<->store call to avoid potential deadlock (or add clear documentation + tests).
- [ ] Add at least one integration replay test that mimics INF-1234 trace.
- [ ] Add feature flag and metrics, with dashboard links in PR description.
- [ ] Author responds to concurrency question and documents eviction heuristics.

End of scratchpad. Will follow up with a cleaned-up PR checklist to paste into the PR description after author addresses comments.

-- Liam
